hypothesis: The walk-forward framework, applied to the real development data, produces chronological, non-overlapping test blocks with the required purge gap, and control models behave as leakage-free validation demands: a memorising model scores exactly chance, a last-label carry-forward model scores at the base rate, and a constant base-rate model reproduces the training prior.
acceptance_criterion: PRE-REGISTERED. (F1) Folds cover the evaluation range exactly once, consecutive, chronological; every fold's gap between the last fitted row and the test start equals horizon + embargo + 1 hours. (F2) Memorising model: every out-of-sample prediction is exactly 0.5 (no test timestamp ever found in training). (F3) Last-label model: out-of-sample accuracy within 3 percentage points of the naive rate max(base rate, 1 - base rate) on the same rows, i.e. no head start from label overlap. (F4) Expanding and rolling layouts produce identical test blocks (so later comparisons are like-for-like). (F5) The scoring 0.1.0 baseline evaluated on the same test blocks reproduces its E001 character (acted-direction accuracy 0.47-0.50) -- a consistency check between the fit-free bench and the walk-forward bench.

dataset.source: E001 replay index + binary 24h labels from the spot snapshot

periods.calibration: framework supports a calibration slice; not used in this verification

target.outcome: close of candle opening at as_of+24h

validation_design.reasoning: labels overlap for H hours; the last H training hours before a test block have outcomes inside the test block; the purge removes them; the embargo adds a margin for serially correlated features and for volatility-scaled thresholds that use trailing completed returns. Test blocks of one quarter balance regime coverage against fold count (~27 folds).

results: ALL FIVE CHECKS PASS. F1: 28 consecutive quarterly test blocks covering 2018-08-29 -> 2025-06-30 exactly once; 27 folds have exactly the required 49h gap; fold 6 has 50h because Binance has no candles 2020-02-19 12:00-15:00 UTC, so the 24h label of reference hour 2020-02-18 12:00 is unavailable and that row is (correctly) dropped -- the gap is never shorter than required. F2: the memorising model returned 0.5 for every one of 59,775 out-of-sample rows (Brier exactly 0.2500): no test hour was ever in its training table. F3: last-label model 0.510 vs naive 0.523 (1.3 points BELOW naive; within 3 points, and in the safe direction) -- the purge removes the head start it would get from overlapping labels. F4: expanding and rolling produce identical test blocks and identical row counts per block. F5: scoring 0.1.0 on the same 59,775 rows: acted-hour accuracy 0.478 (E001 character 0.47-0.50 reproduced), edge +0.11%.
affected_design: The walk-forward bench (agent/research/walkforward.py + model_test.py) is trusted for Phase 9-11. Side finding worth remembering: a constant 'training base rate' model loses to the hindsight naive rate in bear years (2018: 0.462 vs 0.538; 2022: 0.469 vs 0.531) because the majority direction flips -- so the naive rate used in acceptance criteria is a hindsight benchmark and therefore a STRICT one. Reporting fix: the reliability-bucket flag was renamed 'reliable' -> 'enough_rows' because it only means n >= 100, not 'calibrated'.
notes: This is verification, not research. Nothing is learned about Bitcoin here; what is learned is whether the bench can be trusted for Phase 9.
